title: Stale reverse-DNS propagation window causes transient cross-tenant hostname association
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Several Dedicated tenants reported transient hostname misresolution after autoscaler and egress pool resize events. Symptoms included tenant A's egress IP briefly resolving to tenant B's reverse-DNS entry, leading to internal service calls being routed to the wrong tenant during a 30–90s window after scale events. Impact: production requests returned 5xx for affected customers and triggered multiple escalations. This ticket tracks the emergency mitigation, root-cause analysis, and permanent fix to ensure tenant reverse-DNS (PTR) and egress metadata cannot be observed or cached across tenant boundaries during topology transitions.

acceptance_criteria: No cross-tenant PTR or reverse-DNS observations during or after autoscaler/egress-pool-resize events in staging and canary clusters

steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two dedicated tenants (tenant-A, tenant-B) sharing the same egress IP pool in staging
2) Pin a long-lived connection for tenant-A to observe its PTR mapping
3) Trigger autoscaler to resize pool and concurrently allocate new ephemeral SNAT addresses for tenant-B

4) Observe resolver and NAT gateway logs: PTR for tenant-B's new ephemeral IP appears resolvable before control plane updates tenant metadata, causing PTR responses momentarily to reflect stale associations
5) Validate by querying internal name-resolver and verifying reverse lookup mismatch window
root_cause_summary: Race condition between egress metadata propagation in the control plane and PTR records written by the dataplane NAT gateway. When the dataplane allocates an ephemeral SNAT for a tenant and writes PTR, that PTR becomes visible externally before the control plane has atomically updated tenant-to-ip mappings and invalidated other caches, allowing a short window where reverse-DNS points at the wrong tenant.
mitigation_and_fix: Short-term: force synchronous PTR write ordering and a brief quarantine where newly allocated SNATs are only announced to the resolver after control-plane confirmation; applied as a prod-side toggle. Long-term: implement atomic allocation workflow where egress metadata is prepared on the control plane, then published to dataplane with a handshake and publish-subscribe acknowledgement; add automated invalidation hooks for external caches and lower PTR TTLs for ephemeral ranges. Code changes in infra PR 4891 implement the quarantine plus metrics; follow-up PR will rework allocation protocol.
resolution: Partial mitigation deployed 2025-02-19; quarantine feature toggled on in prod for affected clusters and rolling fix under canary as of 2025-02-27. Full atomic allocation workflow targeted for runtime-1.20 (release window Mar 2025).
